cita: Lin et al. (2026). Agentic Harness Engineering: Observability-Driven Automatic Evolution of Coding-Agent Harnesses.
problema: Automating coding-agent harness engineering (system prompt, tools, middleware, skills, memory) is hard because the action space is heterogeneous, raw trajectories bury actionable signal in millions of tokens, and edit effects are hard to attribute, so harness improvement remains a manual, ad-hoc craft that struggles to keep pace with rapidly advancing base models.
mecanismo: Three observability pillars close the loop: component observability exposes seven harness component types (including long-term memory) as explicit versioned files so edits are revertible (WRITE); experience observability (Agent Debugger) distills millions of raw trajectory tokens into a layered, drill-down per-task evidence corpus an Evolve Agent can consume (RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO); decision observability pairs every edit with a self-declared falsifiable prediction in a change manifest, verified against the next round's task-level outcomes — edits that fail their prediction are reverted at file granularity (OLVIDO) while validated ones are committed via git (ACTUALIZACION).
evaluacion: 10 AHE iterations on the full 89-task Terminal-Bench 2 (GPT-5.4 high, ~32h), compared against human-designed harnesses (OpenCode, Terminus-2, Codex) and self-evolving baselines (ACE, Training-Free GRPO); cross-benchmark transfer to SWE-bench-verified (500 tasks) and cross-model transfer to 5 alternate base models, plus a per-component ablation (memory/tools/middleware/prompt) isolating where the gain lives.
numeros_clave: AHE lifts Terminal-Bench 2 pass@1 from 69.7% (seed) to 77.0%, beating Codex (71.9%), ACE (68.9%) and TF-GRPO (72.3%); on SWE-bench-verified it reaches the highest aggregate success (75.6%) while using 12% fewer tokens than the seed and 32%/21% fewer than ACE/TF-GRPO; cross-model transfer yields +5.1 to +10.1pp gains across 3 alternate model families; component ablation shows tools/middleware/long-term-memory each beat the seed alone while the system-prompt-only swap regresses.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: component observability represents every editable harness piece (prompt, tools, middleware, skills, long-term memory) as an explicit file at a fixed mount point with one git commit per edit (§3.1), a concrete instance of typed, versioned narrative-as-truth close to MF's Tier-1 anchor.

reports tokens/trial explicitly (Table2) and shows the evolved harness cuts aggregate tokens by 12-32% versus baselines on a transfer benchmark, external evidence that memory/tool design measurably affects context economy.

decision observability attaches a self-declared, falsifiable prediction to every edit that the next round's task-level outcomes must confirm or the edit is reverted at file granularity (§3.3), a concrete provenance/verification mechanism MF could adopt against silent drift.

notes: Numbers from Table1 (Terminal-Bench 2), Table2 (SWE-bench-verified transfer), Fig.3 (cross-model transfer), Table3 (component ablation, §4.4.1).

cita: Song et al. (2026). SkillOps: Managing LLM Agent Skill Libraries as Self-Maintaining Software Ecosystems.
problema: LLM agent skill libraries accumulate 'skill technical debt' over time — redundant, stale, interface-mismatched, or unvalidated skills that don't break any single task locally but degrade future retrieval, composition and execution reliability; existing skill-based agents only handle task-time retrieval/repair and ignore library-time maintenance.
mecanismo: Each skill is represented as a typed Skill Contract (precondition/operation/artifact/validator/failure-modes) linked into a Hierarchical Skill Ecosystem Graph via typed dependency/compatibility/redundancy/alternative edges (WRITE); a Task-Time loop retrieves and stitches skills through dependency/compatibility constraints with local repair (RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO); a Library-Time loop scores five health dimensions per skill (utility, redundancy, compatibility, failure-risk, validation-gap), propagates risk along dependency edges, then applies typed maintenance actions merge (CONSOLIDACION), retire (OLVIDO) and repair/add-validator (ACTUALIZACION) — nearly rule-based, near-zero LLM cost at library time.
evaluacion: Evaluated on ALFWorld with a 200-2000 skill library built from 229 curated SkillsBench skills plus synthetically degraded variants (six technical-debt patterns), against ReAct, LLM_Skill_Planner, Hybrid_Retrieval, GoS_Style and SkillWeaver baselines on GPT-4o-mini; measures standalone task success, plug-in lift over each baseline, task-time token-cost delta, and library-scale/ablation studies.
numeros_clave: SkillOps_Full reaches 79.5% success on ALFWorld (200-skill library), +8.9pp over the strongest baseline (LLM_Skill_Planner 70.6%); as a plug-in it lifts Hybrid Retrieval by +2.90pp, BM25 by +1.00pp, Dense by +1.12pp; at 2000 skills SkillOps leads the next-best baseline by >31pp; maintenance is token-neutral-to-beneficial (24/35 cells decrease, largest -3.95%) with nearly zero library-time LLM calls.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: the Library-Time Loop explicitly scores utility/redundancy/failure-risk/validation-gap per skill and applies merge/retire/repair actions between tasks (Algorithm2), directly measuring the value of promoting/demoting entries rather than passively accumulating them.

typed Skill Contracts require an explicit Validator field and flag a 'validation gap' when missing (§2), and CGPD propagates upstream risk to catch structurally-sound-looking skills that inherit failure risk — direct evidence for provenance/staleness guarding as a first-class memory dimension.

Table3 explicitly measures task-time token deltas after maintenance (mostly neutral-to-negative) and states the rule-based maintenance pass uses near-zero library-time LLM calls, external evidence that memory-management overhead can be kept near-zero.

notes: Numbers from Table1 (standalone), Table2 (plug-in delta), Table3 (token cost), §5.2 (library-scale stress test).

cita: Fan et al. (2026). Resource2Skills: Distilling Executable Skills from Human-Created Resources for Software Agents.
problema: Existing skill libraries for software agents are hand-written, text-centric, or derived only from an agent's own traces, leaving rich human-created multimodal resources (tutorial videos, repos, articles) largely untapped, even though procedural know-how for creative/commercial software is often best conveyed through demonstration rather than static text.
mecanismo: An offline construction operator distills multimodal resources into typed multimodal skill-wiki entries (structured text, code, visual examples, metadata, provenance — HIBRIDA) organized in a domain-specific hierarchical taxonomy, passing quality gates for dedup/completeness/executability/safety (WRITE/ADMISION); at inference a two-stage MetaBrowse retrieves candidates via BM25 over name/tags/applicability/taxonomy-path then an LLM selects a subset to compose (RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO); when the offline pool lacks coverage, the same construction operator is invoked online as a controlled gap-filler.
evaluacion: Evaluated across 7 authoring domains (Web/Excel/Reaper/PPT/Blender/CAD/UE5) and 4 model backbones (GPT-5.5/5.4/5.4-mini/5.4-nano) against no-skill agents and two off-the-shelf harnesses (ClaudeCode-H, Codex-H), plus ablations on skill-pool scale, wiki organization vs flat text, source mix, and offline-vs-online acquisition, and a blinded human A/B study.
numeros_clave: w/ Skills beats w/o Skills in all 28 main-aggregate model-domain cells, averaging 56.8% vs 45.0% (+11.9pp), and beats the stronger off-the-shelf harness in 26/28 cells; UE5 gains +30 to +40pp; online acquisition adds only +0.7pp on standard tasks but +21.6pp (41.2%->62.8%) on a novel-capability stress test; performance saturates near 200 skills; hierarchical wiki beats flat text by 2.5-8.2pp.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: each skill is a typed multimodal entry with structured text/code/visual fields plus explicit provenance/metadata organized in a domain taxonomy (§3.1), a pattern for combining a typed narrative record with non-text evidence that MF's Tier-1 docs-as-truth could generalize toward.

the hierarchical taxonomy path is used as a first-class retrieval signal alongside name/tags/applicability (§3.3), evidence that organizing a single source of truth by domain structure (not a flat blob) materially narrows and sharpens retrieval.

a domain-specific predicate enforces five acceptance checks (completeness, traceable provenance, deduplication, modality consistency, structural executability) before a distilled candidate enters the wiki (§3.2), guarding the memory store against low-quality or unverifiable entries.

notes: Numbers from Table1 (main comparison), Table2 (offline/online acquisition), Table3 (source-mix ablation), Fig.a (scaling).

cita: Wang et al. (2023). VOYAGER: An Open-Ended Embodied Agent with Large Language Models.
problema: LLM-based embodied agents in open-ended environments (Minecraft) are not lifelong learners: they cannot progressively propose their own tasks, acquire and reuse skills across long horizons, or avoid re-deriving the same routines from scratch, so they plateau and cannot compound capability over time.
mecanismo: An automatic curriculum (LLM-generated, state-conditioned) proposes progressively harder tasks; an iterative prompting loop generates executable JavaScript programs, incorporating environment feedback and execution errors across rounds until an LLM self-verification module confirms task completion, at which point the verified program (WRITE/ADMISION of only successful skills) is added to an ever-growing skill library indexed by the embedding of its natural-language description (HIBRIDA: code + vector index); composable, reusable skills (CONSOLIDACION, since complex skills are built on simpler stored ones) are retrieved by similarity for future tasks.
evaluacion: Evaluated in MineDojo/Minecraft against ReAct, Reflexion and AutoGPT on tech-tree mastery, exploration (unique items discovered), map coverage, and zero-shot generalization to a new world with cleared inventory; ablations remove curriculum, skill library, and each feedback type.
numeros_clave: VOYAGER discovers 3.3x more unique items, travels 2.3x longer distances, unlocks tech-tree milestones up to 15.3x faster (wooden), 8.5x (stone), 6.4x (iron) than baselines, and is the only method to unlock the diamond tool tier (1/3 runs); removing the skill library causes a plateau in later exploration stages; removing self-verification drops discovered items by 73%; GPT-3.5 vs GPT-4 for code generation yields 5.7x fewer unique items.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: the automatic curriculum conditions its next proposed task on the agent's running list of completed/failed tasks and current world state (§2.1), an explicit plan/progress-state record fed back into planning, direct precedent for MF's PLAN-ESTADO anchor.

only self-verified successful programs are committed to the skill library, and complex skills are explicitly built by composing simpler stored ones (§2.2), a canonical example of promoting validated experience into durable, reusable recipes.
the paper reports prompting-iteration counts as an efficiency proxy (Table1/2) rather than tokens/latency directly, relevant context for MF's cost lens but not a direct cost measurement.

notes: Numbers from Table1 (tech tree), Table2 (zero-shot generalization), Fig.9 (ablation studies).

cita: Wang et al. (2023). LDM2: A Large Decision Model Imitating Human Cognition with Dynamic Memory Enhancement.
problema: Standard few-shot prompting for LLM decision-making agents relies on fixed, manually crafted example prompts that cannot generalize to complex or unseen situations and cannot be updated with environment feedback once fixed, so the agent's decision quality is capped by whatever examples were chosen upfront.
mecanismo: A memory-formation stage (WRITE) decomposes human demonstration trajectories into standard state-action tuples (goal, LLM-summarized history, observation, action) clustered by LLM-generated goal/observation indices and stored as batch memories (DOCS-ARCHIVOS); at inference the most relevant tuples are retrieved (RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO) via the goal/observation index to build a dynamic prompt; a memory-refinement stage runs LLM-guided tree exploration to generate multiple candidate decision processes, compares the best-reward path against a memory-only 'ground' path, and adds (ADMISION) the valuable sub-trajectory after the key divergence point back into memory.
evaluacion: Evaluated on WebShop (500 test instructions, score + success rate) and ALFWorld (134 test games, success rate) with GPT-3.5-turbo, against Standard few-shot, ReAct and Reflexion baselines, comparing initial memory (LDM2-In) vs refined memory (LDM2-In+Re) against a human-expert upper bound.
numeros_clave: On WebShop, LDM2 reaches score 71.8 / success-rate 40.8% with initial memory and 72.4 / 41.6% after refinement, versus Standard 62.7/29.6%, ReAct 67.1/39.6%, Reflexion 68.4/40.2% (human expert 82.1/59.6%).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: the LLM-summarized historical information hτ explicitly tracks 'the decision stage it has reached' to guide future actions (§3.2), a lightweight plan-state summary distinct from raw history that MF's PLAN-ESTADO anchor could reuse.

memory refinement compares an explored best-reward decision path against the memory-only ground path and back-fills only the valuable divergent sub-trajectory into memory (§3.3), a targeted consolidation pattern (add only the delta that beat the baseline) rather than bulk logging.

batching trajectories (batch size 50-100) to keep each memory shard within context length is a pragmatic context-budget workaround (§3.2) relevant to MF's economy lens though not measured as a cost metric.

notes: Numbers from Table1 (WebShop score/SR); ALFWorld results follow in §5 (not fully captured at read cutoff, but WebShop numbers ground evidencia_tipo).

cita: Roth et al. (2024). Pairing Analogy-Augmented Generation with Procedural Memory for Procedural Q&A.
problema: LLMs struggle to synthesize disparate pieces of information into a coherent multi-step plan for procedural tasks in specialized or unfamiliar domains (e.g. a library newer than the model's training cutoff), and standard few-shot/RAG retrieval surfaces noisy or insufficiently related examples when the query wording doesn't match stored procedures.
mecanismo: A procedural-memory store embeds whole linear procedures (input/output/ordered-steps, WRITE) built from a formal chain-graph representation and retrieved via K-nearest cosine similarity (VECTOR); a query generator decomposes the goal into a high-level outline and rewrites it into up to N=4 sub-questions (HyDE-style), each retrieving and being answered against K analogical procedures by an answer-generator LLM (RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO); an iterative LLM self-critic then revises the composed answer for up to T=3 cycles before returning the final procedure.
evaluacion: Evaluated on LCStep (a new LangChain-tutorial dataset chosen because it postdates the test LLM's training cutoff), RecipeNLG, and CHAMP, via LLM-based pairwise comparison against Zero-Shot, Few-Shot, RAG and ReAct baselines (plus a blind human study on RecipeNLG), with a full ablation removing the query generator, answer generator, and critic refinement in all combinations.
numeros_clave: AAG wins over RAG in 69.64% of LCStep pairwise comparisons (loss 12.50%, ties 17.86%) and 85.70% of RecipeNLG comparisons (loss 7.60%); a blind human study on RecipeNLG found 56% preferred AAG recipes vs 16% RAG (28% tie); removing the query generator (NO QG) drops the AAG-win rate to 71.43%/80.05% (still positive but reduced).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: the ablation study (Table1, NO QG/NO AG/NO CR rows) measures exactly how much each retrieval/analogy component contributes to output quality via pairwise LLM and human evaluation, direct external evidence for treating retrieval design as a measured layer rather than an assumed one.

query rewriting into sub-questions before searching the vector memory (§4.2, HyDE-style) is a derived/cached intermediate representation built purely to sharpen retrieval, a pattern relevant to MF's TIER-INDICE derived-index-as-cache anchor.

inference-time cost of the multi-query, multi-cycle refinement pipeline is only briefly addressed (appendix reference) rather than being a first-class measured axis in the main body read, relevant context but not a strong signal either way.

notes: Numbers from Table1 (LLM pairwise evaluation) and §5.5 (human study, RecipeNLG).
